text_blocks.snippet: In Addison's disease, also known as adrenal insufficiency, potassium levels can be elevated (hyperkalemia) due to the body's inability to regulate electrolytes properly. This is because the adrenal glands, specifically the hormone aldosterone, play a crucial role in maintaining the balance of sodium and potassium.
snippet_highlighted_words: potassium levels can be elevated (hyperkalemia) due to the body's inability to regulate electrolytes properly

list.title: Adrenal Glands and Electrolytes:
list.snippet: The adrenal glands, located on top of the kidneys, produce hormones like cortisol and aldosterone. Aldosterone is particularly important for regulating sodium and potassium levels in the body.

list.title: Aldosterone Deficiency:
list.snippet: In Addison's disease, the adrenal glands are damaged, leading to insufficient production of aldosterone.

list.title: Electrolyte Imbalance:
list.snippet: Without enough aldosterone, the kidneys retain potassium and excrete more sodium than usual. This results in high potassium levels (hyperkalemia) and low sodium levels (hyponatremia).
